questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me, the most crucial aspect of choosing my study destination was the specialisation I would be granted based on the choice, as well as the provided courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The orientation week for incoming students was well-organised, clear and helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance as I have not requested it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Even though I did not make use of it, it was very helpful of the university to provide incoming international students with transport from the airport.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to find suitable housing off campus, every landlord I contacted was always very helpful and quick to respond. However, I would recommend any future students start looking for accommodation as soon as they can because there weren't many options left during the summer already.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend living off campus as it is cheaper than living in the student accommodation provided by the university, especially since you can find places that are equally close or sometimes even closer to the campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: At the end of the summer the University was faster to respond, but the response time during the period of June-July was quite long.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Fortunately, I did not have to register for classes myself, it was done by the University. However, there is some paperwork to be filled out in order to proceed with the exchange which was more tiresome due to the lack of connection of Bangor University to Mobility Online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As I have not used any kind of help from the University, I do not know what kind of help was available. However, it  was made clear to us who the course coordinators were and I am sure they would provide us with help if needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was not able to choose which classes I take, I had to follow the course plan. As such, I was registered automatically and did not have to worry about it.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would definitely start the paperwork as early as possible as the communication between Universities can sometimes take some time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Although the quality of the modules varied, I had a very satisfying experience overall. There were multiple smaller assignments with feedback throughout the year rather than having only one big exam at the end of the semester, which I found very helpful in developing my academic skills.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Although the level of the courses was adequate to the degree level, the lecturers made sure that people from different backgrounds had the same understanding of the basics of the material as well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As the course itself was smaller, it felt much more personal than at UCPH. Additionally, half of the assignments were not group assignments and therefore more individual feedback was provided. However, it was also less structured as every week had a different schedule, unlike at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Research Planning & Communications, Conservation Science, Agriculture & the Environment

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: Research Planning & Communications, Dissertation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Conservation Science was a great module I can wholeheartedly recommend - not only does it cover a wide range of topics within animal and plant conservation, it also provides a lot of additional resources and topical examples.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Even if you have your own personal insurance/the European health card, when getting a student visa you must pay the insurance fee (which you can later get a refund for) of about 6000 dkk.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The accommodation was more expensive than I expected - the prices are comparable with Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a variety of societies available for students, from all the different disciplines - sports, music and theatre, research, volunteering, and more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are so many student-led organisations that anybody can find something for themselves. I would definitely recommend going to Serendipity - a day at the University where all the organisations promote themselves.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of attractions for nature lovers - hiking trails, lakes, and wildlife reserves.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to adjust - the University feels very welcoming and provides a lot of opportunities to bond with other students. However, there are definitely fewer socialising places in the traditional sense, such as clubs, than there are in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would definitely check out the student organisations as almost all of them do weekly socials in pubs etc, which is a great opportunity to socialise with others.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't think there were too many cultural differences - most of them came down to the language and slang not formerly known to me. I think one thing I noticed is that strangers are far more likely to approach you and that British people tend to be a little friendlier/louder than Copenhageners.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The locals were very welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make sure you calculate your budget correctly, as it is very hard to find a job in Bangor. I would also start the paperwork and searching for accommodation as soon as possible. I would also definitely recommend to part take in University life as much as possible, because the University offers a lot of wonderful opportunities, academic, career but also cultural and socialising as well.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bring good hiking shoes and rainproof clothing! :) Umbrellas are useless here due to the wind.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of the experience was the people I got to meet - both locals and internationals. I also believe the study-life balance is well-kept.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during the exchange was definitely the finances and budgeting.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I definitely recommend Bangor University as an exchange destination!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
